Apple has updated the privacy policy for the Apple Store app, adding provisions related to an unreleased virtual shopping assistant. Details below.

Apple is expanding the use of AI in its retail operations

According to findings by MacRumors, the Apple Store app and its privacy page now include a new section titled "Virtual Shopping Assistant," which reads as follows:

In other words, the Apple Store app may soon incorporate a chatbot that uses user data to provide personalised responses, helping users make purchase decisions.

Apple says it will strip personally identifiable information from conversations before sharing them with unnamed partners to generate assistant responses — a practice that strongly suggests third-party models will power at least part of the experience.

Conversation histories will be kept inside the app for users to revisit, and will also be retained for Apple's business analytics. A new "Chat Improvements" setting lets users opt in or out independently of having their conversations used to improve the Virtual Shopping Assistant.

The wording in Apple's privacy policy suggests that the virtual assistant will initially launch only in selected countries and regions, likely debuting in English-speaking markets before rolling out to other languages and locations.

Months before this news came to light, Apple had already integrated an AI chatbot into its internal Sales Coach app to provide sales and technical resources for the company's retail partners. Accessible via the "Ask" tab, the chatbot draws on Apple's official training materials and documentation to answer questions.

Previously, Bloomberg also reported that Apple is testing a system called "Live Notes" at some retail stores. The system uses AI to record, transcribe and summarise Genius Bar service sessions, allowing staff to focus on helping customers without being distracted by taking notes.
